refs.quote: COZAAR (losartan potassium) is an angiotensin II receptor blocker acting on the AT 1 receptor subtype.

tall_man.note: Not listed in FDA/ISMP Tall Man list; generic name lowercase per EXTRACTION.md

refs.quote: COZAAR ® is indicated for the treatment of hypertension in adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older, to lower blood pressure. Lowering blood pressure lowers the risk of fatal and nonfatal cardiovascular (CV) events, primarily strokes and myocardial infarction.
The usual starting dose of COZAAR is 50 mg once daily. The dosage can be increased to a maximum dose of 100 mg once daily as needed to control blood pressure

regimens.dose_text: Usual starting dose: 50 mg orally once daily; may increase to maximum 100 mg once daily. A starting dose of 25 mg once daily is recommended for patients with possible intravascular depletion (e.g., on diuretic therapy) or mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment.

regimens.indication: Hypertension (Pediatric Patients >= 6 Years with eGFR >= 30 mL/min/1.73m2)

refs.quote: The usual recommended starting dose is 0.7 mg per kg once daily (up to 50 mg total) administered as a tablet or a suspension [see Dosage and Administration (2.5) ] . Dosage should be adjusted according to blood pressure response. Doses above 1.4 mg per kg (or in excess of 100 mg) daily have not been studied in pediatric patients

regimens.dose_text: 0.7 mg/kg once daily (up to 50 mg total) as tablet or compounded suspension; adjust according to BP response (doses >1.4 mg/kg or >100 mg daily not studied). Not recommended in pediatric patients <6 years or eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m2.

regimens.dose_text: Starting dose: 50 mg orally once daily. Add hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily and/or increase losartan to 100 mg once daily (then HCTZ 25 mg daily) based on blood pressure response.

renal_impairment.description: No dose adjustment is necessary in patients with renal impairment unless the patient is also volume depleted. Neither losartan nor its active metabolite can be removed by hemodialysis.

hepatic.value: In patients with mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment, the recommended starting dose is 25 mg once daily (plasma concentrations of losartan and active metabolite were 5x and 1.7x higher). Not studied in severe hepatic impairment.

refs.quote: In patients with mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment the recommended starting dose of COZAAR is 25 mg once daily. COZAAR has not been studied in patients with severe hepatic impairment

Losartan and its principal active metabolite block the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II by selectively blocking the binding of angiotensin II to the AT 1 receptor found in many tissues, (e.g., vascular smooth muscle, adrenal gland).

mg_safety.note: ARBs do not impair neuromuscular transmission and are generally considered safe in myasthenia gravis.

value.instructions: COZAAR film-coated tablets can be dispersed in water/Ora-Plus/Ora-Sweet SF to prepare a 2.5 mg/mL oral suspension per Section 2.5, suitable for enteral administration.

refs.locator: Section 2.5 Preparation of Suspension (for 200 mL of a 2.5 mg/mL suspension)
refs.quote: Add 10 mL of Purified Water USP to an 8 ounce (240 mL) amber polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottle containing ten 50 mg COZAAR tablets. Immediately shake for at least 2 minutes. Let the concentrate stand for 1 hour and then shake for 1 minute to disperse the tablet contents.

pgx.value: CYP2C9: Subjects with a specific rare defect in CYP2C9 do not metabolize losartan to its active carboxylic acid metabolite, which is responsible for most of its AT1 receptor antagonism.

refs.quote: Subjects who do not metabolize losartan to active metabolite have been shown to have a specific, rare defect in cytochrome P450 2C9. These data suggest that the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite is mediated primarily by P450 2C9 and not P450 3A4.
Metabolic and Nutrition: Hyponatremia.
Nervous system disorders: Somnolence, headache, sleep disorders, paresthesia, migraine.
Digestive: Hepatitis.
Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥2% and greater than placebo) are: dizziness, upper respiratory infection, nasal congestion, and back pain.

value.drug_or_class: Aliskiren and Dual RAS Blockade (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aliskiren)
value.effect: Dual blockade of the RAS is associated with increased risks of hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure).
value.management: Do not coadminister aliskiren with COZAAR in patients with diabetes; avoid aliskiren in patients with GFR < 60 mL/min. In general, avoid combined use of RAS inhibitors.

refs.locator: Section 7.4 Dual Blockade of the Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS)
refs.quote: In general, avoid combined use of RAS inhibitors. Closely monitor blood pressure, renal function, and electrolytes in patients on COZAAR and other agents that affect the RAS. Do not coadminister aliskiren with COZAAR in patients with diabetes. Avoid use of aliskiren with COZAAR in patients with renal impairment (GFR <60 mL/min).

value.effect: Coadministration of losartan with other drugs that raise serum potassium levels may result in hyperkalemia.
value.management: Monitor serum potassium in patients receiving concomitant potassium-raising drugs.

refs.quote: Coadministration of losartan with other drugs that raise serum potassium levels may result in hyperkalemia. Monitor serum potassium in such patients.

value.effect: Increases in serum lithium concentrations and lithium toxicity have been reported during concomitant administration with ARBs.
value.management: Monitor serum lithium levels during concomitant use.

value.effect: May result in deterioration of renal function including possible acute renal failure (especially in elderly, volume-depleted, or renal-impaired patients) and attenuate antihypertensive effect.
value.management: Monitor renal function periodically in patients receiving losartan and NSAID therapy.

refs.locator: Section 7.3 Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) Including Selective Cyclooxygenase-2 Inhibitors (COX-2 Inhibitors)
refs.quote: In patients who are elderly, volume-depleted (including those on diuretic therapy), or with compromised renal function, coadministration of NSAIDs, including selective COX-2 inhibitors, with angiotensin II receptor antagonists (including losartan) may result in deterioration of renal function, including possible acute renal failure.

value.effect: Fluconazole decreased AUC of active metabolite by ~40% and increased losartan AUC by ~70%; rifampin decreased AUC of losartan and active metabolite by 30% and 40%, respectively.
value.management: Monitor antihypertensive response when co-administering with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors or rifampin.

refs.quote: However, rifampin has been shown to decrease the AUC of losartan and its active metabolite by 30% and 40%, respectively. Fluconazole, an inhibitor of cytochrome P450 2C9, decreased the AUC of the active metabolite by approximately 40%, but increased the AUC of losartan by approximately 70% following multiple doses.

WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY When pregnancy is detected, discontinue COZAAR as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus

Oligohydramnios in pregnant women who use drugs affecting the renin-angiotensin system in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy can result in the following: reduced fetal renal function leading to anuria and renal failure, fetal lung hypoplasia, skeletal deformations, including skull hypoplasia, hypotension, and death.

tier.note: 5-axis synthesis: Boxed Warning for fetal toxicity requiring immediate discontinuation upon pregnancy detection; 2nd/3rd trimester RAS blockade causes oligohydramnios, fetal renal failure, skull/lung hypoplasia, and neonatal death.

It is not known whether losartan is excreted in human milk, but significant levels of losartan and its active metabolite were shown to be present in rat milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects on the nursing infant, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.
